title: Explicit positive-rate codes below the Plotkin point
formal: For every fixed finite adversarial channel \(A\) with rational polyhedral input and noise constraints, and every fixed integer \(L\ge2\), does the existence of a nonconfusable completely positive order-\(L\) distribution with admissible input marginal imply a uniform deterministic polynomial-time encodable family of positive-rate \((L-1)\)-list-decodable codes for that same channel? The alphabets, transition rule, constraints and list bound are fixed as blocklength grows; all terms and the allowed blocklength convention are defined below.
why: The information-theoretic criterion identifies when a channel permits a linear amount of information with a fixed ambiguity bound. Making that criterion explicit would turn a broad existence theorem into efficiently usable encoders without changing the channel or relaxing the list bound.
status_note: Explicit construction is open in the ITCS 2020 source. The 2025 zero-rate theorem and checked 2025 revised derandomization results, including the work published at STOC 2026, do not by their stated guarantees settle this fixed-channel formulation. Later checks through 2026-09-16 are bounded.

progress.text: The source gives the completely positive achievability condition and leaves explicit positive-rate constructions as an open question.
Tight upper and lower bounds determine the scale of zero-rate code sizes above the threshold for the stated list-recovery parameters. This concerns the opposite side of the positive-rate boundary.
The subspace-design preprint gives explicit folded codes preserving local properties of random linear codes; Theorem 1.4 uses a field size proportional to blocklength.
The checked revised preprint gives explicit codes for local coordinate-wise linear properties with an enlarged constant alphabet; Remark 1.4 states that alphabet tradeoff.

importance.reason: This asks whether the general information-theoretic criterion for positive-rate communication against a fixed adversarial channel has an efficient deterministic realization. A universal answer would explain the gap between random existence and explicit error-correcting objects across many channel models while preserving a fixed small list bound.
importance.basis: Individual reading of the ITCS 2020 channel definitions, completely positive achievability criterion and explicit-construction question, with later zero-rate and derandomization results checked for scope.

sentences: A fixed adversarial channel restricts the types of transmitted words and noise words and transforms each input symbol through a specified table.
The source gives a completely positive distribution criterion ensuring that positive-rate codes with a fixed list bound exist.
The question asks whether every channel satisfying that criterion also admits deterministic encoders running in polynomial time in blocklength.
The card fixes a finite-description channel model, preserves its alphabet and list bound, and specifies uniformity and the permitted infinite set of blocklengths.
A resolution would connect a general information-theoretic feasibility criterion with explicit error-correcting constructions across many adversarial channel models.

definitions:
A channel \(A=(X,\Lambda_X,S,\Lambda_S,Y,W)\) has finite alphabets \(X=\{1,\ldots,a\}\), \(S=\{1,\ldots,b\}\), \(Y=\{1,\ldots,c\}\), where \(a\ge2\) and \(b,c\ge1\). Its deterministic transition rule is a table \(W:X\times S\to Y\). For a finite set \(T\), write \(\Delta(T)=\{p\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{T}:\sum_{t\in T}p(t)=1\}\). The nonempty sets \(\Lambda_X\subseteq\Delta(X)\) and \(\Lambda_S\subseteq\Delta(S)\) are closed rational polytopes, each given by finitely many linear equalities and non-strict inequalities with rational coefficients. The table, alphabet sizes, signed integer numerators and positive denominators have ordinary binary encodings. These are fixed channel data, independent of blocklength.

The type of \(u\in T^n\) is \(\tau_u(t)=|\{j:u_j=t\}|/n\). An input word \(x\in X^n\) is admissible if \(\tau_x\in\Lambda_X\). Given \(x\), any \(s\in S^n\) with \(\tau_s\in\Lambda_S\) is allowable noise, and the output is \(y_j=W(x_j,s_j)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,n\). The adversary may choose the entire noise word with knowledge of the entire input word. There is no causality restriction, random channel transition, feedback, shared randomness, insertion or deletion.

A code \(C\subseteq X^n\) consists of admissible input words. It is \((L-1)\)-list-decodable when, for every \(y\in Y^n\), at most \(L-1\) distinct words \(x\in C\) admit an allowable noise word producing \(y\). Different candidate input words may use different noise words. This is a zero-error combinatorial guarantee over every output; it imposes no running-time bound on finding the list.

The promise on \(A,L\) is that there exist a probability vector \(p\in\Lambda_X\), a finite integer \(h\ge1\), probability vectors \(p_1,\ldots,p_h\in\Delta(X)\), and real numbers \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_h\ge0\) with \(\sum_j\lambda_j=1\), such that
\[
Q(x_1,\ldots,x_L)=\sum_{j=1}^{h}\lambda_j\prod_{i=1}^{L}p_j(x_i),
\qquad p=\sum_{j=1}^{h}\lambda_jp_j,
\]
is nonconfusable. This is the completely positive distribution condition. The component distributions \(p_j\) need not individually satisfy the input constraints; their common resulting marginal \(p\) must.

Precisely, \(Q\) is confusable if there exists a joint probability distribution \(Z\) on \(X^L\times S^L\times Y\) whose marginal on \(X^L\) is \(Q\), whose \(i\)-th noise-coordinate marginal belongs to \(\Lambda_S\) for every \(1\le i\le L\), and which gives probability one to \(y=W(x_i,s_i)\) simultaneously for all \(i\). Nonconfusable means that no such \(Z\) exists. These distributions are real probability vectors; the promise does not require their entries to be rational or supplied to an encoder.

An explicit positive-rate family means that there exist a rational \(R>0\), an infinite set \(B\subseteq\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\) of blocklengths, two finite deterministic Turing-machine programs \(H,E\), and constants \(K,t\ge1\), with the following properties. On unary input \(1^n\), \(H\) decides whether \(n\in B\) in at most \(K(n+1)^t\) bit operations. For every \(n\in B\), set \(k_n=\lceil Rn\rceil\). On input \((1^n,m)\), with \(m\in\{0,1\}^{k_n}\), the encoder \(E\) outputs \(E_n(m)\in X^n\) in at most \(K(n+1)^t\) bit operations, using binary encodings for output symbols. The map \(E_n\) is injective and its image \(C_n\) is an admissible \((L-1)\)-list-decodable code. Thus the rate \(\log_2|C_n|/n\), measured in information bits per channel use, is at least \(R\).

The programs, constants, rate and infinite length set may depend on the fixed \(A,L\), but not on the particular blocklength or message. Both programs are uniform across lengths and have no advice, oracle, random bits or precomputed codebook supplied as input. The cost bound includes all preprocessing done on that input. No polynomial dependence on the binary description length of a varying channel is required, and there is no demand for a uniform algorithm that produces the programs from the channel. An infinite decidable set of lengths permits divisibility restrictions from exact type constraints; no positive density of those lengths is assumed. The output alphabet is exactly \(X\); replacing it or changing the channel is not allowed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of this universal explicit-construction assertion, including polynomial bit complexity, positive rate and the fixed \((L-1)\) list bound, or a complete Lean proof of its negation for the stated class of channels. A random existence proof, exhaustive construction taking time polynomial only in the exponentially large codebook, or a construction after changing the alphabet does not meet the assertion. Efficient list decoding is not an additional requirement. The asymptotic polynomial-resource and positive-rate requirements do not carry a \(1/100\) numerical tolerance.

context_blocks.text: Section 18, item 4 asks for explicit positive-rate codes whenever a nonconfusable completely positive distribution exists. Theorem 47 already establishes positive-rate existence; the unresolved part is explicit construction.

This card specifies the deterministic finite-alphabet channel branch used in the paper. It explicitly restricts the convex type constraints to fixed closed rational polytopes, so that the channel has finite exact data. It does not claim to cover arbitrary real, length-dependent constraints or stochastic transition rules.

“Explicit” is interpreted as one polynomial-time encoder per fixed channel and list bound, on an infinite polynomial-time recognizable set of lengths. The source’s positive-rate convention permits an infinite sequence of blocklengths. The length-set and Turing-machine clauses make that convention algorithmic, without requiring a code for every length or an efficient list-decoding procedure.

The completely positive condition involves mixtures of independent equal-marginal products. Confusability allows a different noise explanation for each of the candidate codewords, provided that all explanations yield the same output. This is more general than a single Hamming-distance threshold.

The 2025 zero-rate result bounds code size above the list-decoding or list-recovery threshold. Its matching constructions in that regime do not provide positive-rate families for every channel below the threshold.

Later explicit constructions reproduce broad classes of local properties of random linear codes. The checked AEL-based theorem increases the alphabet, and the checked folded Reed–Solomon construction uses an alphabet growing with length. These statements do not by themselves supply codes for every fixed channel and fixed alphabet in this card.

checked_sources: Read ITCS 2020 Section 9 Definitions 30–42, Section 12 Theorem 47 and surrounding achievability scope, Section 18 item 4, and Appendix Definition 93. The channel law is deterministic in the studied model and list bound L-1 is a fixed constant.

Checked the normalization of completely positive tensors: normalizing each nonzero nonnegative vector and absorbing its L-th power of total mass into the mixing weight gives a convex combination of product distributions with common marginal equal to their weighted mean.

Read ITCS 2025 Section 1.1 Theorems 1–2 and the Section 1.2 code-construction discussion. Its matching size bounds concern p above the threshold and do not assert positive-rate explicit codes for arbitrary fixed channels.

Read arXiv:2510.06185v2 Section 1.1 Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.4: the explicit construction increases the alphabet. Confirmed version date 19 November 2025, rather than treating a 2026 citation as a newly posted result.

Read arXiv:2510.13777v1 Section 1.1.1 Theorems 1.3–1.4 and the concurrent-work comparison on pages 5–7. The stated explicit subspace-design application has field size Theta(sn), not a construction over each preassigned channel alphabet. Verified STOC 2026 follow-up publication on a coauthor primary publications page.
